subject: [hw] R1 finding F14 (V40, LOW): 64-bit mmap offset overflow can pass the shmem range checks
body:
From the R1 review of DONE V40 (vcu/test_v40 PASS 1161/1161; n2vcu.c read; no other finding).

F14 (low): vcu/n2vcu.c:1168-1208 (vcu_mmap_ioctl) computes `uint64_t end = offset + len;` and then tests `offset >= BASE && end <= BASE + RANGE` for the MAP_SHMEM_ALLOC/COMMIT/MM/CACHEABLE/PA ranges. A guest mmap64 offset near UINT64_MAX wraps `end` to a small value, so the range test can pass; the return value is `v->dmem_guest + (uint32_t)(offset - BASE)` (or vcu_dma_guest with a truncated PA), i.e. a guest address outside the DMEM/range the caller asked for. The guest already owns its address space, so this is not a host escape; it is a mapping-validation bug (the guest gets a mapping it should not, and n2vcu_map_dm_addr would later reject the same address).

Repro shape: len=0x1000, offset=0xfffffffffffff000 -> end=0, `offset >= VCU_SHMEM_ALLOC_BASE` and `end <= BASE+RANGE` both true -> returns dmem_guest + 0x7ffff000. Expected: MAP_FAILED/0.

Fix: reject `offset > UINT64_MAX - len` before computing end, or require `offset < (1ull << 40)` (all real bases are below 0x900000000) before the range tests; then the existing end tests are safe.

Everything else in V40 looks sound: SET/GET_OBJECT use bounded waits with abort/stop_request, the handler runs without the lock, the 80-byte share copies are field-checked, alloc/free/cache use the kernel bounds (len > 0, <= 128 MiB, 512 slots), the GCE list is clamped to CMDQ_CMD_MAX and every poll/wait has a deadline, and the register mmap only accepts the three documented windows. V40 is accept with this low finding in review/r1/FINDINGS.md.
